title: Adaptive EKS control-plane provisioner with canary health prober
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a new Terraform module that provisions the Redwood Private EKS control plane with adaptive health probing and a lightweight canary promotion flow. This module should: 1) provision control-plane primitives (IAM roles, EKS cluster control plane config, nodegroup or managed node bootstrap hooks when needed) and network primitives (VPC subnets, route tables, NAT), or accept existing VPC inputs; 2) embed a declarative 'prober' submodule that runs small canary clusters and control-plane API probes post-upgrade to validate kube-apiserver latency, etcd replication health, and cloud-controller-manager responses; 3) include upgrade hooks and rollback safety toggles to coordinate safe rolling upgrades of managed control-plane components; 4) expose outputs for operational tooling: healthscore metric endpoints, preflight dry-run summary, and required IAM statements; 5) support a non-destructive 'plan-and-verify' mode to run probes against a blue/green control-plane candidate in dedicated temporary namespaces before switching routing; 6) integrate with console telemetry by emitting tags and a standard CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics schema for the prober; 7) be idempotent, smaller blast radius by default, with explicit flags for destructive operations. Acceptance criteria: - Terraform module passes terraform validate and unit tests in CI. - Can run 'apply' in a dev VPC and produce a cluster with probing resources that report healthy within 15 minutes. - Module provides a canary workflow (create-candidate -> run-probers -> promote-or-fail) documented and automatable via CI. - Observability: prober metrics available in metrics endpoint with labels cluster_id/env/component. - Rollout safety: at least two independent safety gates (canary success threshold + manual approval) before promotion. - Backwards compatibility: module can accept existing cluster inputs for customers who only want prober added. Out-of-scope for this ticket: deep automation of node-autoscaling policies and on-prem bare-metal variants (separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Module validates and builds with terraform 1.5+
CI tests include mocked AWS API calls and basic plan diffs
A dev apply creates a cluster + prober that reports 'healthy' within 15 minutes
Canary promotion flow documented and runnable via a simple CLI wrapper
Prober metrics exported with cluster_id and env labels to the metrics endpoint
Module supports 'attach-only' mode to add probers to existing clusters
implementation_notes: Prefer smaller, composable submodules: network, iam, eks_controlplane, prober
Use terraform null_resource with local-exec for lightweight prober bootstrap until we ship a containerized operator
Prober should run a combination of: kube-apiserver latency checks, controller-manager recon syncs, etcd leader count and write-read sanity tests
Expose a TF var 'prober_mode' with values [disabled, standalone_job, operator]
Add a toggle 'protective_mode' default true that prevents destructive replacements unless explicitly set
Emit an output 'preflight_summary_url' that links to a signed S3 object produced by CI for human review
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Prober false-positives block upgrades — Mitigation: allow manual override and add a configurable retry/backoff policy
Risk: IAM scope creep — Mitigation: generate minimal ARNs and document required permissions with example policies
Risk: Long apply times for full VPC builds — Mitigation: separate network creation into an optional submodule and support import of existing VPCs
Risk: Metrics sampling could leak PII — Mitigation: strip sensitive labels and only emit cluster_id hashed in telemetry
rollout_plan: Week 1: Implement core TF module scaffolding + network/iam submodules
Week 2: Add prober null_job implementation and basic probes; unit tests
Week 3: CI integration and canary promotion flow automation script; internal doc and runbook
Week 4: Run controlled canary on staging, collect metrics and failure modes
Week 5: Security review and handbook update, then ship to private customers behind feature flag
